trust_boundaries: Public Internet to API Gateway Boundary
API Gateway to Auth Layer Boundary
API Gateway to App Layer Boundary
Auth Service to Redis Cache Boundary
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-hosted multi-tier REST API platform servicing external public clients via an API Gateway routing layer.

threat_actors.name: External Cybercrime Group
threat_actors.motivation: Financial gain through unauthorized access to user accounts, data theft, and API abuse.
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Publicly exposed API Gateway endpoints via credential stuffing or web application vulnerability exploitation.
non_capabilities: No direct access to internal VPC networks
No physical access to cloud datacenter infrastructure
No access to internal source code repositories or CI/CD pipelines

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider
threat_actors.motivation: Data exfiltration, corporate espionage, or operational disruption.
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Direct network access to internal Auth Service, Redis, or App Server from within the internal network segment.
non_capabilities: No root control over cloud infrastructure hypervisor
No access to underlying cloud provider global control plane

attack_paths.impact: Exploitation of API Gateway vulnerabilities leading to unauthorized request routing bypass or remote code execution.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: API Gateway is directly reachable over the public internet and processes untrusted incoming HTTP requests.

attack_paths.impact: Attacker leverages compromised credentials against AuthService to issue valid session tokens and gain unauthorized API access.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Authentication endpoints are publicly accessible through the API Gateway, exposing them to credential stuffing.

attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of session tokens, authentication secrets, or cached user data stored unencrypted in Redis.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires lateral movement into the Auth Layer or an unauthenticated Redis instance on internal networks.

attack_paths.impact: Interception and tampering of unencrypted internal traffic between API Gateway and App Server.
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires positioning on the internal network path between the API Gateway and App Server.

mitigations.control_name: Web Application Firewall and API Security Gateway
Multi-Factor Authentication and Rate Limiting on Auth Endpoints
Redis Access Authentication, Network Isolation, and Encryption at Rest
Internal Mutual TLS (mTLS) between Gateway and Backend Services

findings.severity_rationale: Publicly exposed API Gateway vulnerabilities can allow direct access to internal network components.
Lack of robust rate limiting or MFA on AuthService allows account takeover via credential stuffing.
Unauthenticated or unencrypted Redis instances risk token compromise if internal perimeter is breached.
Unencrypted communication between internal API Gateway and App Server permits network eavesdropping.
